chunks: He (peace be upon him) said to one of his companions during an illness he had contracted:

May Allah make what is of your complaint a writing-off of your sins, for indeed illness has no reward in itself, but it erases sins and makes them fall like leaves. And indeed the reward lies in saying with the tongue and acting with the hands and feet. And certainly Allah, Glorified is He, admits by the truthfulness of intention and the sound inner self whom He wills from among His servants into Paradise.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of illness in Shia Islam and how does it differ from the reward of worship?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the passive expiation of sins through illness, which 'strips away' faults like leaves falling from a tree, and the active acquisition of reward through deliberate worship. This hadith highlights the Shia emphasis on the primacy of sincere intention (ikhlas) as the decisive factor for divine acceptance, bridging the gap between physical suffering and spiritual elevation.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 42. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said to one of his companions during his sickness:

May Allāh make your illness a means for writing off your sins, because there is no reward for sickness but that it erases sins and makes them fall like (dried) leaves. Reward lies in saying by the tongue and doing something with the hands and feet. Certainly, Allāh, the Glorified, admits into Paradise by virtue of truthfulness of intention and chastity of heart to whomsoever He wishes from among His creatures.
